Page iii
Introduction
The
following
document
is
intended
to
provide
details
of
the
REST
API
interface
for
the
Resource Activation and Configuration Management. The intent of this API is to provide a
consistent
and
standardized
mechanism
to
activate,
configure,
and
manage
the
state
of
Resources in the network.
It includes the model definition as well as all available operations.
Scope
The Resource Activation and Configuration API (TMF702) provides a means for a system to
activate and configure network resources, and to track the status of those operations. The
API distinguishes between two categories of resource:
•
PhysicalResource
– tangible hardware assets such as routers, switches, antennas, and
cables.
•
LogicalResource
– software-defined or virtual resources such as IP addresses, MSISDN
numbers, VLANs, and software licenses.
The
API
also
provides
a
Monitor
resource
that
enables
asynchronous
tracking
of
long-
running activation and configuration operations.
Relationship to Resource Inventory (TMF639)
The Resource Activation and Configuration API complements the Resource Inventory API
(TMF639). While TMF639 provides a read-oriented view of the current state of resources in
the
inventory,
TMF702
is
focused
on
the
lifecycle
management
of
those
resources
—
specifically
their
activation,
configuration
changes,
and
decommissioning.
Resources
activated through TMF702 are typically reflected in the inventory managed by TMF639.
NOTE
The
API
model
for
the
Resource
entity
used
in
TMF702
is
essentially
the
same as that used in TMF639 Resource Inventory.
Operations
Resource
Activation
and
Configuration
API
performs
the
following
operations
on
the
resources :
•
Retrieve an entity or a collection of entities depending on filter criteria
•
Partial update of an entity (including updating rules)

Page 1
•
Create an entity (including default values and creation rules)
•
Delete an entity (for administration purposes)
•
Manage notification of events

Sample Use Cases
Reader will find example of use cases using the Resource Activation and Configuration API
in the "How to use ODA – Using Open APIs to realize Use Cases v29.0.0 (IG1228)" document.
Activate a subscriber’s mobile number (Use Case 1)
When
a
customer
subscribes
to
a
mobile
service,
the
operator’s
Order
Management
system invokes the Resource Activation and Configuration API to activate the MSISDN (a
LogicalResource) on the network. The API call creates or updates the resource record, sets
its
administrativeState
to
unlocked
,
operationalState
to
enabled
,
and
usageState
to
active
.
A
ResourceCreateEvent
or
ResourceAttributeValueChangeEvent
notification
is
published
to
downstream
systems.
Commission and configure new network equipment (Use Case 2)
After physical installation of new network equipment (a PhysicalResource such as a router
or
base
station),
the
Network
Operations
System
calls
the
Resource
Activation
and
Configuration
API
to
provision
the
device’s
initial
configuration
—
including
firmware
version,
port
settings,
and
operational
policies
captured
as
activationFeature
items.
The
Monitor
resource
is
used
to
track
the
asynchronous
completion
of
the
provisioning
workflow.
Update resource configuration after maintenance (Use Case 3)
Following
a
planned
maintenance
window,
the
operations
system
uses
the
PATCH
operation
on
the
Resource
Activation
and
Configuration
API
to
update
the
administrativeState
back
to
unlocked
,
operationalState
to
enabled
,
and
usageState
to
active
.
A
ResourceStateChangeEvent
notification
is
published
to
subscribing systems to signal the return to service.
Decommission a resource at end of life (Use Case 4)
When a physical device reaches its end of life or a logical number is no longer required, the
Resource
Activation
and
Configuration
API
is
called
to
set
administrativeState
to
locked
and
operationalState
to
disabled
before the resource record is permanently
deleted. A
ResourceDeleteEvent
notification is published to allow downstream inventory
and billing systems to reconcile their records.
Asynchronous resource activation monitoring (Use Case 5)
For
resource
activation
requests
that
involve
long-running
or
external
processes
(e.g.,
provisioning a circuit across multiple domains), the API creates a Monitor resource linked to
Resource Activation and Configuration User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 3
the original request. The client polls the Monitor or receives a
MonitorStateChangeEvent
notification when the activation completes or fails. The Monitor records both the original
request and the system’s response for audit purposes.

Support of polymorphism and extension
patterns
Support of polymorphic collections and types and schema based extension is provided by
means
of
a
list
of
generic
meta-attributes
that
we
describe
below.
Polymorphism
in
collections occurs when entities inherit from base entities, for instance a PhysicalResource
and LogicalResource inheriting properties from the abstract Resource entity.
Generic
support
of
polymorphism
and
pattern
extensions
is
described
in
the
TMF
API
Guidelines, Part 2 (TMF630).
The
@type
attribute
provides
a
way
to
represent
the
actual
class
type
of
an
entity.
For
example, within a list of Resource instances some may be instances of PhysicalResource
where other could be instances of LogicalResource. The @type gives this information. All
resources and sub-resources of this API have a @type attributes that must be provided.
The @referredType can be used within reference entities (like for instance an ResourceRef
object)
to
explicitly
denote
the
actual
entity
type
of
the
referred
class.
Notice
that
in
reference
entities
the
@type
denotes
the
class
type
of
the
reference
itself,
such
as
PhysicalResourceRef or LogicalResourceRef, and not the class type of the referred object.
The @schemaLocation property can be used in resources to allow specifying user-defined
properties of an Entity or to specify the expected characteristics of an entity.
The
@baseType
attribute
gives
a
way
to
provide
explicitly
the
base
of
class
of
a
given
resource that has been extended.

enumeration
for

the
administrative state attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-

by

for

Use
of
the

is
administratively
permitted
to
existing
instances
of
use
only.
While

remains
in

the
managed
object
to
revert
to
the
unlocked
state;
'unlocked':
The

is

permitted
to

for
its
users;

of

alarmStatus
A ResourceAlarmStatusType [0..*]. Value enumeration for
the 'resourceAlarmStatus' of a Resource; the alarm status
attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-T M.3701) represents
the
severity
status
of
fault
for
a
resource;
it
is
multi-
valued
and
read-only
by
management
functions,
each
value
represents
an
existing
severity;
defined
values:
'underRepair':
The
resource
is
currently
being
repaired;
'critical': One or more critical alarms indicating a fault have
been
detected
in
the
resource,
and
have
not
been
cleared;
'major':
One
or
more
major
alarms
indicating
a
fault
have
been
detected
in
the
resource,
and
have
not
yet
been
cleared;
'minor':
One
or
more
minor
alarms
indicating a fault have been detected in the resource, and
have
not
yet
been
cleared;
'alarmOutstanding':
One
or
more
alarms
have
been
detected
in
the
resource.
The
condition may or may not be disabling. If the operational
state
is
'enabled',
additional
attributes,
particular
to
the
managed object class, may indicate the nature and cause
of
the
condition
and
the
services
that
are
affected.
ENUMERATED with values:
* underRepair
* critical
* major
* minor
* alarmOutstanding

availabilityStatus
A
ResourceAvailabilityStatusType.
Value
enumeration
for
the
'resourceAvailabilityStatus'
of
a
Resource;
the
availability status attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-T
M.3701)
represents
the
availability
of
the
resource
for
either carrying service or for being in other states, such as
in
testing;
it
is
single
valued
and
read-only
by
management
functions;
defined
values:
'inTest':
The
resource
is
undergoing
a
test
procedure.
If
the
administrative
state
is
'locked'
or
'shuttingDown',
then
normal users are precluded from using the resource, and
the
controlStatus
attribute
has
the
value
'reservedForTest'.
Tests
that
do
not
exclude
additional
users can be present in any operational or administrative
state
but
the
'reservedForTest'
condition
should
not
be
present;
'failed':
The
resource
has
an
internal
fault
that
prevents
it
from
operating.
The
operational
state
is
'disabled';
'powerOff':
The
resource
requires
power
to
be
applied
and
is
not
powered
on.
The
operational
state
is
'disabled';
'online':
The
resource
is
available
for
use.
The
operational
state
is
'enabled';
'offline':
The
resource
requires a routine operation to be performed to place it
on line and make it available for use. The operation may
be manual or automatic, or both. The operational state is
'disabled'; 'offDuty': The resource has been made inactive
by
an
internal
control
process
in
accordance
with
a
predetermined
time
schedule.
Under
normal
conditions
the
control
process
can
be
expected
to
reactivate
the
resource
at
some
scheduled
time,
and
it
is
therefore
considered
to
be
optional.
The
operational
state
is
'enabled' or 'disabled'; 'dependency': The resource cannot
operate
because
some
other
resource
on
which
it
depends
(i.e.,
a
resource
not
represented
by
the
same
managed
object)
is
unavailable.
The
operational
state
is
'disabled';
'degraded':
The
service
available
from
the
resource is degraded in some respect, such as in speed or
operating
capacity.
Failure
of
a
test
or
an
unacceptable
performance measurement has established that some or
all services are not functional or are degraded due to the
presence
of
a
defect.
However,
the
resource
remains
available
for
service,
either
because
some
services
are
satisfactory or because degraded service is preferable to

controlStatus
A ResourceControlStatusType. Value enumeration for the
'resourceControlStatus' of a Resource; the control status
attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-T M.3701) indicates
that the resource is under some kind of control; it is single
valued and read-only by management functions; defined
values: 'subjectToTest': The resource is available to normal
users, but tests may be conducted on it simultaneously at
unpredictable
times,
which
may
cause
it
to
exhibit
unusual
characteristics
to
users;
'partOfServicesLocked':
This
value
indicates
whether
a
manager
has
administratively
restricted
a
particular
part
of
a
service
from the user(s) of a resource. The administrative state is
'unlocked'.
Examples
are
incoming
service
barred,
outgoing service barred, write locked by media key, read
locked;
'reservedForTest':
The
resource
has
been
made
administratively unavailable to normal users because it is
undergoing a test procedure. The administrative state is
'locked';
'suspended':
Service
has
been
administratively
suspended
to
the
users
of
the
resource.
The
resource
may
retain
knowledge
of
current
users
and/or
requests
for
usage,
depending
upon
the
managed
object
class
definition, but does not resume performing services until
the
suspended
condition
is
revoked.
The
administrative
state is 'unlocked'. ENUMERATED with values:
* subjectToTest
* partOfServicesLocked
* reservedForTest
* suspended

proceduralStatus
A
ResourceProceduralStatusType.
Value
enumeration
for
the
'resourceProceduralStatus'
of
a
Resource;
the
procedural status attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-T
M.3701) represents a sequence of phases through which
the
resource
needs
to
progress;
it
is
single
valued
and
read-only
by
management
functions;
defined
values:
'initializationRequired':
The
resource
requires
initialization
to
be
invoked
by
the
manager
before
it
can
perform
its
normal
functions,
and
this
procedure
has
not
been
initiated.
The
manager
may
be
able
to
invoke
such
initialization
through
an
action.
The
operational
state
is
'disabled';
'notInitialized':
The
resource
requires
initialization
before
it
can
perform
its
normal
functions,
and
this
procedure
has
not
been
initiated.
The
resource
initializes
itself
autonomously,
but
the
operational
state
may be either 'disabled' or 'enabled', depending upon the
managed object class definition; 'initializing': The resource
requires
initialization
before
it
can
perform
its
normal
functions, and this procedure has been initiated but is not
yet complete. The operational state may be 'disabled' or
'enabled',
depending
upon
the
managed
object
class
definition;
'reporting':
The
resource
has
completed
some
processing
operation
and
is
notifying
the
results
of
the
operation,
e.g.,
a
test
process
is
sending
its
results.
The
operational state is 'enabled'; 'terminating': The resource is
in a termination phase. If the resource does not reinitialize
itself
autonomously,
the
operational
state
is
'disabled'.
Otherwise, the operational state may be either 'disabled'
or
'enabled',
depending
upon
the
managed
object
class
definition. ENUMERATED with values:
* initializationRequired
* notInitialized
* initializing
* reporting
* terminating

resourceSpecification
A
ResourceSpecificationRef.
Resources
are
physical
or
non-physical
components
(or
some
combination
of
these)
within
an
enterprise’s
infrastructure
or
inventory.
They
are
typically
consumed
or
used
by
services
(for
example
a
physical
port
assigned
to
a
service)
or
contribute to the realization of a Product (for example, a
SIM
card).
They
can
be
drawn
from
the
Application,
Computing
and
Network
domains,
and
include,
for
example, Network Elements, software, IT systems, content
and
information,
and
technology
components.
A
ResourceSpecification
is
an
abstract
base
class
for
representing
a
generic
means
for
implementing
a
particular
type
of
Resource.
In
essence,
a
ResourceSpecification
defines
the
common
attributes
and
relationships
of
a
set
of
related
Resources,
while
Resource
defines
a
specific
instance
that
is
based
on
a
particular ResourceSpecification.

CalendarPeriod sub-resource fields
The CalendarPeriod schema represents a period of time within a calendar, defining various
attributes such as the applicable day, timezone, hour period, and status. It is designed to
capture information about the availability or status of a calendar period, which can be used
in scheduling, booking, or resource allocation applications.
day
A DayOfWeekType. Possible values for the days of the
week. ENUMERATED with values:
* mon
* tue
* wed
* thu
* fri
* sat
* sun
* weekdays
* weekend
hourPeriod
A HourPeriod [0..*]. Start and end time range in 24-hour
HH:mm format.
status
A String [1]. Indication of the availability of the calendar
period (e.g.: available, booked, etc.).
timeZone
A String. Indication of the timezone applicable to the
calendar information in ISO 8601 timezone: either 'Z' for
UTC or an offset like +02:00 or -05:30.

ExternalIdentifier sub-resource fields
An identification of an entity that is owned by or originates in a software system different
from
the
current
system,
for
example
a
ProductOrder
handed
off
from
a
commerce
platform
into
an
order
handling
system.
The
structure
identifies
the
system
itself,
the
nature
of
the
entity
within
the
system
(e.g.
class
name)
and
the
unique
ID
of
the
entity
within the system. It is anticipated that multiple external IDs can be held for a single entity,
e.g. if the entity passed through multiple systems on the way to the current system. In this
case
the
consumer
is
expected
to
sequence
the
IDs
in
the
array
in
reverse
order
of
provenance, i.e. most recent system first in the list.
externalIdentifierType
A String. Type of the identification, typically would be the
type of the entity within the external system.
id
A String [1]. Identification of the entity within the external
system.
owner
A String. Name of the external system that owns the
entity.

ResourceSpecificationRef sub-resource fields
Resources are physical or non-physical components (or some combination of these) within
an
enterprise’s
infrastructure
or
inventory.
They
are
typically
consumed
or
used
by
services (for example a physical port assigned to a service) or contribute to the realization
of a Product (for example, a SIM card). They can be drawn from the Application, Computing
and Network domains, and include, for example, Network Elements, software, IT systems,
content
and
information,
and
technology
components.
A
ResourceSpecification
is
an
abstract base class for representing a generic means for implementing a particular type of
Resource.
In
essence,
a
ResourceSpecification
defines
the
common
attributes
and
relationships of a set of related Resources, while Resource defines a specific instance that
is based on a particular ResourceSpecification.
href
A String. The URI of the referred entity.
id

name

version
A String. Resource Specification version.

PhysicalResource sub-resource fields
Resource Activation and Configuration User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 34
Physical resource is a type of resource that describes the common set of attributes shared
by all concrete physical resources (e.g. EQUIPMENT) in the inventory.
activationFeature
A Feature [0..*]. Configuration features; see TMF664
Resource Function Activation API.
administrativeState
A ResourceAdministrativeStateType. Value enumeration
for the 'resourceAdministrativeState' of a Resource; the
administrative state attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-
T M.3701) represents permission to use ('unlocked') or
prohibition against using ('locked') the resource imposed
through the management services; it is single valued and
read-write by management functions; defined values:
'locked': The resource is administratively prohibited from
performing services for its users; 'shutdown': Use of the
resource is administratively permitted to existing
instances of use only. While the system remains in the
shutting down state the manager may at any time cause
the managed object to revert to the unlocked state;
'unlocked': The resource is administratively permitted to
perform services for its users; this is independent of its
inherent operability. ENUMERATED with values:
* locked
* unlocked
* shuttingDown
Resource Activation and Configuration User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 35
alarmStatus
A ResourceAlarmStatusType [0..*]. Value enumeration for
the 'resourceAlarmStatus' of a Resource; the alarm status
attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-T M.3701) represents
the severity status of fault for a resource; it is multi-
valued and read-only by management functions, each
value represents an existing severity; defined values:
'underRepair': The resource is currently being repaired;
'critical': One or more critical alarms indicating a fault have
been detected in the resource, and have not been
cleared; 'major': One or more major alarms indicating a
fault have been detected in the resource, and have not
yet been cleared; 'minor': One or more minor alarms
indicating a fault have been detected in the resource, and
have not yet been cleared; 'alarmOutstanding': One or
more alarms have been detected in the resource. The
condition may or may not be disabling. If the operational
state is 'enabled', additional attributes, particular to the
managed object class, may indicate the nature and cause
of the condition and the services that are affected.
ENUMERATED with values:
* underRepair
* critical
* major
* minor
* alarmOutstanding
allocationStatus
A ResourceAllocationStatusType. Values for the
'allocationStatus' of a Resource; for example: 'available',
'reserved', 'allocated' and 'partiallyAllocated'.
attachment
An AttachmentRef [0..*]. A list of references to
attachments associated with this resource.
Resource Activation and Configuration User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 36
availabilityStatus
A ResourceAvailabilityStatusType. Value enumeration for
the 'resourceAvailabilityStatus' of a Resource; the
availability status attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-T
M.3701) represents the availability of the resource for
either carrying service or for being in other states, such as
in testing; it is single valued and read-only by
management functions; defined values: 'inTest': The
resource is undergoing a test procedure. If the
administrative state is 'locked' or 'shuttingDown', then
normal users are precluded from using the resource, and
the controlStatus attribute has the value
'reservedForTest'. Tests that do not exclude additional
users can be present in any operational or administrative
state but the 'reservedForTest' condition should not be
present; 'failed': The resource has an internal fault that
prevents it from operating. The operational state is
'disabled'; 'powerOff': The resource requires power to be
applied and is not powered on. The operational state is
'disabled'; 'online': The resource is available for use. The
operational state is 'enabled'; 'offline': The resource
requires a routine operation to be performed to place it
on line and make it available for use. The operation may be
manual or automatic, or both. The operational state is
'disabled'; 'offDuty': The resource has been made inactive
by an internal control process in accordance with a
predetermined time schedule. Under normal conditions
the control process can be expected to reactivate the
resource at some scheduled time, and it is therefore
considered to be optional. The operational state is
'enabled' or 'disabled'; 'dependency': The resource cannot
operate because some other resource on which it
depends (i.e., a resource not represented by the same
managed object) is unavailable. The operational state is
'disabled'; 'degraded': The service available from the
resource is degraded in some respect, such as in speed or
operating capacity. Failure of a test or an unacceptable
performance measurement has established that some or
all services are not functional or are degraded due to the
presence of a defect. However, the resource remains
available for service, either because some services are
satisfactory or because degraded service is preferable to
no service at all. Object specific attributes may be defined

powerConsumingState
A ResourcePowerConsumingStateType. Value
enumeration for the 'resourcePowerConsumingState' of a
Resource; the power consuming state attribute (defined
by ITU-T M.3701) indicates the power consuming policy of
the resource represented by the managed object, it is
single valued and read-write by management functions.;
defined values: 'fullPower': The resource runs in full power
and will not consider power saving. If a large device
contains parts that also support this attribute, when the
container object set to full power state, all its parts shall
turn into full power state; 'powerSaving': The resource is
(or may be) partially running to save power; depending on
how much the payload is lower than the maximum
capacity of the resource, the degree of saving will be
automatically decided by the resource. If power saving is
not supported by the resource, attempting to change to
this state will have the same effect as full power state. If a
large device contains parts that also support this
attribute, when the container object is set to power saving
state, its parts may still remain in full power state. But if
one of the parts turns into power saving state, the
container object shall turn into power saving state;
'sleeping': The resource is not running but keeps a
snapshot of its memory before sleeping, and can resume
running mode quickly. In this mode, the power is only
consumed to meet the need of maintaining the memory. If
it is not supported by the resource, attempting to change
to this state will result in a failure; 'shutdown': The
resource has been powered off and does not consume
any more power; if it is not supported by the resource,
attempting to change to this state will result in a failure.
ENUMERATED with values:
* fullPower
* powerSaving
* sleeping
* shutdown

proceduralStatus
A ResourceProceduralStatusType. Value enumeration for
the 'resourceProceduralStatus' of a Resource; the
procedural status attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-T
M.3701) represents a sequence of phases through which
the resource needs to progress; it is single valued and
read-only by management functions; defined values:
'initializationRequired': The resource requires initialization
to be invoked by the manager before it can perform its
normal functions, and this procedure has not been
initiated. The manager may be able to invoke such
initialization through an action. The operational state is
'disabled'; 'notInitialized': The resource requires
initialization before it can perform its normal functions,
and this procedure has not been initiated. The resource
initializes itself autonomously, but the operational state
may be either 'disabled' or 'enabled', depending upon the
managed object class definition; 'initializing': The resource
requires initialization before it can perform its normal
functions, and this procedure has been initiated but is not
yet complete. The operational state may be 'disabled' or
'enabled', depending upon the managed object class
definition; 'reporting': The resource has completed some
processing operation and is notifying the results of the
operation, e.g., a test process is sending its results. The
operational state is 'enabled'; 'terminating': The resource is
in a termination phase. If the resource does not reinitialize
itself autonomously, the operational state is 'disabled'.
Otherwise, the operational state may be either 'disabled'
or 'enabled', depending upon the managed object class
definition. ENUMERATED with values:
* initializationRequired
* notInitialized
* initializing
* reporting
* terminating

resourceSpecification
A ResourceSpecificationRef. Resources are physical or
non-physical components (or some combination of
these) within an enterprise’s infrastructure or inventory.
They are typically consumed or used by services (for
example a physical port assigned to a service) or
contribute to the realization of a Product (for example, a
SIM card). They can be drawn from the Application,
Computing and Network domains, and include, for
example, Network Elements, software, IT systems, content
and information, and technology components. A
ResourceSpecification is an abstract base class for
representing a generic means for implementing a
particular type of Resource. In essence, a
ResourceSpecification defines the common attributes and
relationships of a set of related Resources, while Resource
defines a specific instance that is based on a particular
ResourceSpecification.

standbyStatus
A ResourceStandbyStatusType. Value enumeration for the
'resourceStandbyStatus' of a Resource; the standby
status attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-T M.3701)
represents the working mode for standby objects, i.e.
whether it is providing service or standby as a back-up
resource; it is single valued and read-only by management
functions; defined values: 'hotStandby': The resource is
not providing service, but is operating in synchronism with
another resource that is to be backed-up (e.g., a
computer shadowing another computer). A resource with
a hot standby status will be immediately able to take over
the role of the resource to be backed up, without the
need for initialization activity, and will contain the same
information as the resource to be backed up;
'coldStandby': The resource is to back up another
resource, but is not synchronized with that resource. A
resource with a cold standby status will not be
immediately able to take over the role of a resource to be
backed up, and will require some initialization activity;
'providingService': The back up resource is providing
service and is backing up another resource. ENUMERATED
with values:
* hotStandby
* coldStandby
* providingService

the 'resourceAlarmStatus' of a Resource; the alarm status

the severity status of fault for a resource; it is multi-

more alarms have been detected in the resource. The
condition may or may not be disabling. If the operational
state is 'enabled', additional attributes, particular to the
managed object class, may indicate the nature and cause
of the condition and the services that are affected.

for

state

The

requires a routine operation to be performed to place it

activationFeature
A Feature [0..*]. Configuration features; see TMF664
Resource Function Activation API.
administrativeState
A ResourceAdministrativeStateType. Value enumeration
for the 'resourceAdministrativeState' of a Resource; the
administrative state attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-
T M.3701) represents permission to use ('unlocked') or
prohibition against using ('locked') the resource imposed
through the management services; it is single valued and
read-write by management functions; defined values:
'locked': The resource is administratively prohibited from
performing services for its users; 'shutdown': Use of the
resource is administratively permitted to existing
instances of use only. While the system remains in the
shutting down state the manager may at any time cause
the managed object to revert to the unlocked state;
'unlocked': The resource is administratively permitted to
perform services for its users; this is independent of its
inherent operability. ENUMERATED with values:
* locked
* unlocked
* shuttingDown
Resource Activation and Configuration User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 81
alarmStatus
A ResourceAlarmStatusType [0..*]. Value enumeration for
the 'resourceAlarmStatus' of a Resource; the alarm status
attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-T M.3701) represents
the severity status of fault for a resource; it is multi-
valued and read-only by management functions, each
value represents an existing severity; defined values:
'underRepair': The resource is currently being repaired;
'critical': One or more critical alarms indicating a fault have
been detected in the resource, and have not been
cleared; 'major': One or more major alarms indicating a
fault have been detected in the resource, and have not
yet been cleared; 'minor': One or more minor alarms
indicating a fault have been detected in the resource, and
have not yet been cleared; 'alarmOutstanding': One or
more alarms have been detected in the resource. The
condition may or may not be disabling. If the operational
state is 'enabled', additional attributes, particular to the
managed object class, may indicate the nature and cause
of the condition and the services that are affected.
ENUMERATED with values:
* underRepair
* critical
* major
* minor
* alarmOutstanding

availabilityStatus
A ResourceAvailabilityStatusType. Value enumeration for
the 'resourceAvailabilityStatus' of a Resource; the
availability status attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-T
M.3701) represents the availability of the resource for
either carrying service or for being in other states, such as
in testing; it is single valued and read-only by
management functions; defined values: 'inTest': The
resource is undergoing a test procedure. If the
administrative state is 'locked' or 'shuttingDown', then
normal users are precluded from using the resource, and
the controlStatus attribute has the value
'reservedForTest'. Tests that do not exclude additional
users can be present in any operational or administrative
state but the 'reservedForTest' condition should not be
present; 'failed': The resource has an internal fault that
prevents it from operating. The operational state is
'disabled'; 'powerOff': The resource requires power to be
applied and is not powered on. The operational state is
'disabled'; 'online': The resource is available for use. The
operational state is 'enabled'; 'offline': The resource
requires a routine operation to be performed to place it
on line and make it available for use. The operation may be
manual or automatic, or both. The operational state is
'disabled'; 'offDuty': The resource has been made inactive
by an internal control process in accordance with a
predetermined time schedule. Under normal conditions
the control process can be expected to reactivate the
resource at some scheduled time, and it is therefore
considered to be optional. The operational state is
'enabled' or 'disabled'; 'dependency': The resource cannot
operate because some other resource on which it
depends (i.e., a resource not represented by the same
managed object) is unavailable. The operational state is
'disabled'; 'degraded': The service available from the
resource is degraded in some respect, such as in speed or
operating capacity. Failure of a test or an unacceptable
performance measurement has established that some or
all services are not functional or are degraded due to the
presence of a defect. However, the resource remains
available for service, either because some services are
satisfactory or because degraded service is preferable to
no service at all. Object specific attributes may be defined
Resource Activation and Configuration User Guide

category
DEPRECATED

controlStatus
A ResourceControlStatusType. Value enumeration for the
'resourceControlStatus' of a Resource; the control status
attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-T M.3701) indicates
that the resource is under some kind of control; it is single
valued and read-only by management functions; defined
values: 'subjectToTest': The resource is available to normal
users, but tests may be conducted on it simultaneously at
unpredictable times, which may cause it to exhibit unusual
characteristics to users; 'partOfServicesLocked': This
value indicates whether a manager has administratively
restricted a particular part of a service from the user(s) of
a resource. The administrative state is 'unlocked'.
Examples are incoming service barred, outgoing service
barred, write locked by media key, read locked;
'reservedForTest': The resource has been made
administratively unavailable to normal users because it is
undergoing a test procedure. The administrative state is
'locked'; 'suspended': Service has been administratively
suspended to the users of the resource. The resource may
retain knowledge of current users and/or requests for
usage, depending upon the managed object class
definition, but does not resume performing services until
the suspended condition is revoked. The administrative
state is 'unlocked'. ENUMERATED with values:
* subjectToTest
* partOfServicesLocked
* reservedForTest
* suspended

externalIdentifier
An ExternalIdentifier [0..*]. An identification of this
resource that is owned by or originates in a software
system different from the current system. The structure
identifies the system itself, the nature of the resource
within the system and the unique ID of the resource within
the system. It is anticipated that multiple external IDs can
be held for a single resource, e.g. if the resource passed
through multiple systems on the way to the current
system.
href
A String. Hyperlink reference.
id
A String. Unique identifier.
intent
An IntentRef. Intent reference, for when Intent is used by
other entities.
lifecycleState
A ResourceLifecycleStateType. Value enumeration for the
'resourceLifecycleState' of a Resource; the lifecycle state
attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-T M.3701) represents
the planned and tracked state of a physical or logical
resource; it is single valued and read-write by
management functions; defined values: 'planned',
'installed', 'pendingRemoval'. ENUMERATED with values:
* planned
* installed
* pendingRemoval
name
A String. The name of the resource.
note
A Note [0..*]. A list of notes associated with this resource.
operationalState
A ResourceOperationalStateType. Value enumeration for
the 'resourceOperationalState' of a Resource; the
operational state attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-T
M.3701) tracks whether or not the resource is installed and
working; it is single valued and read-only by management
functions; defined values: 'disabled': The resource is totally
inoperable and unable to provide service to the user(s);
'enabled': The resource is partially or fully operable and
available for use. ENUMERATED with values:
* enabled
* disabled
Resource Activation and Configuration User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 85
place
A RelatedPlaceRef [0..*]. A list of references to places
related to this Resource, differentiated by their role (e.g.,
installation place, usage place).
proceduralStatus
A ResourceProceduralStatusType. Value enumeration for
the 'resourceProceduralStatus' of a Resource; the
procedural status attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-T
M.3701) represents a sequence of phases through which
the resource needs to progress; it is single valued and
read-only by management functions; defined values:
'initializationRequired': The resource requires initialization
to be invoked by the manager before it can perform its
normal functions, and this procedure has not been
initiated. The manager may be able to invoke such
initialization through an action. The operational state is
'disabled'; 'notInitialized': The resource requires
initialization before it can perform its normal functions,
and this procedure has not been initiated. The resource
initializes itself autonomously, but the operational state
may be either 'disabled' or 'enabled', depending upon the
managed object class definition; 'initializing': The resource
requires initialization before it can perform its normal
functions, and this procedure has been initiated but is not
yet complete. The operational state may be 'disabled' or
'enabled', depending upon the managed object class
definition; 'reporting': The resource has completed some
processing operation and is notifying the results of the
operation, e.g., a test process is sending its results. The
operational state is 'enabled'; 'terminating': The resource is
in a termination phase. If the resource does not reinitialize
itself autonomously, the operational state is 'disabled'.
Otherwise, the operational state may be either 'disabled'
or 'enabled', depending upon the managed object class
definition. ENUMERATED with values:
* initializationRequired
* notInitialized
* initializing
* reporting
* terminating

relatedParty
A RelatedPartyRefOrPartyRoleRef [0..*]. A list of Parties or
PartyRoles related to this resource, differentiated by their
role (e.g., owner, user, installer).
resourceCharacteristic
A Characteristic [0..*]. A list of Characteristics of this
resource.
Characteristic can be instantiated as
* BooleanArrayCharacteristic
* BooleanCharacteristic
* IntegerArrayCharacteristic
* IntegerCharacteristic
* NumberArrayCharacteristic
* NumberCharacteristic
* ObjectArrayCharacteristic
* ObjectCharacteristic
* StringArrayCharacteristic
* StringCharacteristic
resourceOrderItem
A RelatedResourceOrderItem [0..*]. A list of resource order
items related to this resource.
resourceRelationship
A ResourceRelationship [0..*]. A list of relationships
between this resource and other resources, differentiated
by relationshipType.
resourceSpecification
A ResourceSpecificationRef. Resources are physical or
non-physical components (or some combination of
these) within an enterprise’s infrastructure or inventory.
They are typically consumed or used by services (for
example a physical port assigned to a service) or
contribute to the realization of a Product (for example, a
SIM card). They can be drawn from the Application,
Computing and Network domains, and include, for
example, Network Elements, software, IT systems, content
and information, and technology components. A
ResourceSpecification is an abstract base class for
representing a generic means for implementing a
particular type of Resource. In essence, a
ResourceSpecification defines the common attributes and
relationships of a set of related Resources, while Resource
defines a specific instance that is based on a particular
ResourceSpecification.

supportingResource
A ResourceRefOrValue [0..*]. A collection of resources that
support this resource (bundling, link Resource
Specification).
unknownStatus
A Boolean. The unknown status attribute (defined by ITU-
T X.731/ITU-T M.3701) indicate that the state of the
resource represented by the managed object is unknown.
It is single valued and read-only by management
functions.
usageState
A ResourceUsageStateType. Value enumeration for the
'resourceUsageState' of a Resource; the usage state
attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-T M.3701) tracks
whether the resource is currently in use and if it can
accept additional users or not; it is single-valued and
read-only by management functions; defined values: 'idle':
The resource is not currently in use; 'active': The resource
is in use, and has sufficient spare operating capacity to
provide for additional users simultaneously; 'busy': The
resource is in use, but it has no spare operating capacity
to provide for additional users at this instant.
ENUMERATED with values:
* idle
* active
* busy
validFor
A TimePeriod. A period of time, either as a deadline
(endDateTime only) a startDateTime only, or both.

enumeration

the
administrative state attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-

to

alarmStatus
A ResourceAlarmStatusType [0..*]. Value enumeration for
the 'resourceAlarmStatus' of a Resource; the alarm status
attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-T M.3701) represents
the
severity
status
of
fault
for
a
resource;
it
is
multi-
valued
and
read-only
by
management
functions,
each
value
represents
an
existing
severity;
defined
values:
'underRepair':
The
resource
is
currently
being
repaired;
'critical': One or more critical alarms indicating a fault have
been
detected
in
the
resource,
and
have
not
been
cleared;
'major':
One
or
more
major
alarms
indicating
a
fault
have
been
detected
in
the
resource,
and
have
not
yet
been
cleared;
'minor':
One
or
more
minor
alarms
indicating a fault have been detected in the resource, and
have
not
yet
been
cleared;
'alarmOutstanding':
One
or
more
alarms
have
been
detected
in
the
resource.
The
condition may or may not be disabling. If the operational
state
is
'enabled',
additional
attributes,
particular
to
the
managed object class, may indicate the nature and cause
of
the
condition
and
the
services
that
are
affected.
ENUMERATED with values:
* underRepair
* critical
* major
* minor
* alarmOutstanding

availabilityStatus
A
ResourceAvailabilityStatusType.
Value
enumeration
for
the
'resourceAvailabilityStatus'
of
a
Resource;
the
availability status attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-T
M.3701)
represents
the
availability
of
the
resource
for
either carrying service or for being in other states, such as
in
testing;
it
is
single
valued
and
read-only
by
management
functions;
defined
values:
'inTest':
The
resource
is
undergoing
a
test
procedure.
If
the
administrative
state
is
'locked'
or
'shuttingDown',
then
normal users are precluded from using the resource, and
the
controlStatus
attribute
has
the
value
'reservedForTest'.
Tests
that
do
not
exclude
additional
users can be present in any operational or administrative
state
but
the
'reservedForTest'
condition
should
not
be
present;
'failed':
The
resource
has
an
internal
fault
that
prevents
it
from
operating.
The
operational
state
is
'disabled';
'powerOff':
The
resource
requires
power
to
be
applied
and
is
not
powered
on.
The
operational
state
is
'disabled';
'online':
The
resource
is
available
for
use.
The
operational
state
is
'enabled';
'offline':
The
resource
requires a routine operation to be performed to place it
on line and make it available for use. The operation may
be manual or automatic, or both. The operational state is
'disabled'; 'offDuty': The resource has been made inactive
by
an
internal
control
process
in
accordance
with
a
predetermined
time
schedule.
Under
normal
conditions
the
control
process
can
be
expected
to
reactivate
the
resource
at
some
scheduled
time,
and
it
is
therefore
considered
to
be
optional.
The
operational
state
is
'enabled' or 'disabled'; 'dependency': The resource cannot
operate
because
some
other
resource
on
which
it
depends
(i.e.,
a
resource
not
represented
by
the
same
managed
object)
is
unavailable.
The
operational
state
is
'disabled';
'degraded':
The
service
available
from
the
resource is degraded in some respect, such as in speed or
operating
capacity.
Failure
of
a
test
or
an
unacceptable
performance measurement has established that some or
all services are not functional or are degraded due to the
presence
of
a
defect.
However,
the
resource
remains
available
for
service,
either
because
some
services
are
satisfactory or because degraded service is preferable to

controlStatus
A ResourceControlStatusType. Value enumeration for the
'resourceControlStatus' of a Resource; the control status
attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-T M.3701) indicates
that the resource is under some kind of control; it is single
valued and read-only by management functions; defined
values: 'subjectToTest': The resource is available to normal
users, but tests may be conducted on it simultaneously at
unpredictable
times,
which
may
cause
it
to
exhibit
unusual
characteristics
to
users;
'partOfServicesLocked':
This
value
indicates
whether
a
manager
has
administratively
restricted
a
particular
part
of
a
service
from the user(s) of a resource. The administrative state is
'unlocked'.
Examples
are
incoming
service
barred,
outgoing service barred, write locked by media key, read
locked;
'reservedForTest':
The
resource
has
been
made
administratively unavailable to normal users because it is
undergoing a test procedure. The administrative state is
'locked';
'suspended':
Service
has
been
administratively
suspended
to
the
users
of
the
resource.
The
resource
may
retain
knowledge
of
current
users
and/or
requests
for
usage,
depending
upon
the
managed
object
class
definition, but does not resume performing services until
the
suspended
condition
is
revoked.
The
administrative
state is 'unlocked'. ENUMERATED with values:
* subjectToTest
* partOfServicesLocked
* reservedForTest
* suspended

ResourceSpecificationRef sub-resource fields
Resources are physical or non-physical components (or some combination of these) within
an
enterprise’s
infrastructure
or
inventory.
They
are
typically
consumed
or
used
by
services (for example a physical port assigned to a service) or contribute to the realization
of a Product (for example, a SIM card). They can be drawn from the Application, Computing
and Network domains, and include, for example, Network Elements, software, IT systems,
content
and
information,
and
technology
components.
A
ResourceSpecification
is
an
Resource Activation and Configuration User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 104
abstract base class for representing a generic means for implementing a particular type of
Resource.
In
essence,
a
ResourceSpecification
defines
the
common
attributes
and
relationships of a set of related Resources, while Resource defines a specific instance that
is based on a particular ResourceSpecification.
See
[ResourceSpecificationRef]
for details.

The notification structure for all notifications in this API follow the pattern depicted by the
figure below. A notification event resource (depicted by "SpecificEvent" placeholder) is a
sub class of a generic Event structure containing at least an id of the event occurrence
(eventId), an event timestamp (eventTime), and the name of the resource (eventType). This
notification
structure
owns
an
event
payload
structure
("SpecificEventPayload"
placeholder) linked to the resource concerned by the notification using the resource name
as access field ("resourceName" placeholder).

Uniform API Operation

Remove an Entity

remove a resource
Execute an Action on an
Entity
POST on TASK Resource

execute Task Resources
Other Request Methods
POST on TASK Resource

used to tunnel other request
methods.

API NOTIFICATIONS
For
every
single
of
operation
on
the
entities
use
the
following
templates
and
provide
sample REST notification POST calls.
It is assumed that the Pub/Sub uses the Register and UnRegister mechanisms described in
the REST Guidelines reproduced below.
Register listener
POST /hub
Description
Sets
the
communication
endpoint
address
the
service
instance
must
use
to
deliver
information about its health state, execution state, failures and metrics. Subsequent POST
calls will be rejected by the service if it does not support multiple listeners. In this case
DELETE /api/hub/{id} must be called before an endpoint can be created again.
Behavior
Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 204 if the request was successful.
Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 409 if request is not successful.
Usage Samples
Here’s an example of a request for registering a listener.
Request
POST /api/hub
Accept: application/json
{
 
"callback": "http://in.listener.com"
}
Response
201
Content-Type: application/json
Location: /api/hub/42

Unregister listener
DELETE /hub/{id}
Description
Clears the communication endpoint address that was set by creating the Hub..
Behavior
Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 204 if the request was successful.
Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 404 if the resource is not found.
Usage Samples

Accept: application/json

Publish Event to listener
POST /client/listener
Description
Clears the communication endpoint address that was set by creating the Hub.
Provides
to
a
registered
listener
the
description
of
the
event
that
was
raised.
The
/client/listener url is the callback url passed when registering the listener.
